narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a relay rack: a lacquered paper enclosure, an engraved nameplate, labeled ports, 1px wiring, and a single signal lamp that travels the circuit. The interface is not the subject. The work is. Every section is a panel on the same rack, so a recruiter can trace Senguichet from the mobile app to payment to validation before reading a biography.

The palette is deliberately narrow: paper, ink, one signal amber, and one validated green. There is no violet, no glow, no gradient text, and no skill bar. Depth comes from 1px rules, tonal paper, and two full-bleed charcoal panels reserved for the security and contact arguments. The system is flat by default and physical where it matters: a nameplate with screws, ports that light when a project is linked, a pulse that crosses the circuit once.

The motion grammar is one authored moment, not a layer of entrances. The amber pulse crosses the Senguichet circuit on load; after that, the interface answers the pointer and the keyboard and then stays still. Real evidence leads: the product demo, the mobile presentation, the design mockups labeled as design mockups, the eight certificates, the two timelines. Nothing is presented as proof unless it is traceable.
keyCharacteristics: Paper and charcoal, two grounds, no third.
Amber as signal, never as body text.
1px rules, engraved labels, and a 200px rail that maps the page.
One authored motion: the amber pulse across the Senguichet circuit.
Real demos and real links; design mockups are labeled as design mockups.
One section per screen; equal left and right edges.

rules.name: The Amber Is Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber appears on ports, pulses, bracket rules, and active markers; it never carries body text on paper. If a line needs to be read, it is ink.

rules.name: The Two-Ground Rule
rules.body: There are two grounds: lacquered paper and charcoal ink. The charcoal panels are full-bleed and reserved for the security and contact arguments. No third ground, no gradient sky.

rules.name: The No-Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet and lavender are absent from the system, including the favicon. The bolt is amber on paper.

rules.name: The Mono Is a Tool Rule
rules.body: DM Mono is for data: labels, durations, addresses, dates, measurements. It never sets a paragraph or a headline; monospace is not a costume.

rules.name: The Name Is the Headline Rule
rules.body: The h1 is the name, set in the nameplate. There is no eyebrow, kicker, or job-title label above it.

rules.name: The Balance Rule
rules.body: Display and headline text use text-wrap: balance; do not manually break a headline into a shape.

rules.name: The One-Ground-Per-Screen Rule
rules.body: Each section is a room. No second heading, no next panel, peeks into the current screen at 1440×900.

rules.name: The Rail Is the Map Rule
rules.body: The rail lists the five destinations and the CV. It is the only index; no decorative section numbers elsewhere.

rules.name: The Equal Edges Rule
rules.body: Every block begins and ends on the .wrap lines or the grid columns. Nothing is allowed to hang off one side.

rules.name: The Shadow Is Physical Rule
rules.body: A shadow is an offset under a solid object, not a colored halo. No glow, no 0-offset bloom, no hard offset.

rules.name: The 2px Rule
rules.body: 2px on surfaces. 999px only on status LEDs, circuit ports, and timeline nodes. No large rounded cards.

rules.name: The Evidence Rule
rules.body: Every visual is either the real product or a labeled design mockup. No stock photo, no invented screenshot, no fake verification link.

dos: Do use amber as a signal on ports, pulses, bracket rules, and active markers; keep body text in ink.
Do keep the h1 as the name, set in the nameplate; no eyebrow above it.
Do use 2px radii; reserve 999px for LEDs, ports, and timeline nodes.
Do use 1px rules to structure; the rail, the circuit, and the ledger rows carry the world.
Do keep two grounds: paper and charcoal. Use charcoal only for the security and contact arguments.
Do keep one authored motion: the amber pulse that crosses the Senguichet circuit once.
Do label design mockups as design mockups; use the real demo and mobile presentation.
Do keep the CV and contact one action away.
donts: Don't use violet or lavender anywhere, including the favicon.
Don't use glow, colored halos, or gradient text.
Don't use skill bars, percentages, or progress rings; certifications are validated lines.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; use the inline SVG set.
Don't present a design mockup as a live screenshot.
Don't invent years, verification links, repos, projects, or claims.
Don't add a contact form without a backend; use the honest mailto.
Don't use large rounded cards or nested cards; the ledger rows and panels are the structure.
Don't set long prose in DM Mono.
